name: Hidden doubles play: doubles matches in the last 7 days and at this event
definition: For each player before the match: D7 = doubles matches played on clock days d-7..d-1 (d = this match's best-estimate day), any level, split into D7_here (same event) and D7_else, with doubles sets as a load variant; x = log1p(D7)_A - log1p(D7)_B and the two parts separately. Men 2013-17 (no doubles days on disk): 1[entered in this event's doubles draw] (known at the draw) and doubles matches at the previous event.
mechanism: Singles prices, our model and sets_14d see singles only. Doubles is competitive match play in today's conditions without the survival/form signal of singles wins, so it separates rhythm from survival behind the unpriced sets_14d and U-138; its load is invisible to a singles trader.
data_paths: data/dump/points/tennislive/listed.parquet (discipline, start_utc, player1_members, player2_members); data/studies/lower_level_evidence/system/stage0/C0_now/evidence/crosswalk_tennislive.csv (names to Stage 0 ids); data/dump/matches/sackmann_archive/atp/atp_matches_doubles_2010..2020.parquet; data/dump/points/wta/ (API doubles 2019-26); data/studies/match_timing/timing.parquet (obs)
coverage_note: TennisLive: 170,241 doubles rows 2018-26 both tours; 95.8% of member-rows map to a Stage 0 id by name. Frame matches where exactly one player played doubles in days -7..-1: men 0.30-0.38 (2018-24), 0.25 / 0.24 (2025 / 2026); women 0.33-0.38, 0.36 / 0.30. Men 2013-20 (Sackmann, by level): exactly one player in the same event's doubles draw in 0.43-0.45. Women before 2018 not held. (data/studies/unpriced_leads/team/rhythm_body/prevalence.txt)
model_overlap: none (rough x: R2 0.034 men / 0.023 women on the 49 non-price inputs; corr with sets_14d 0.03-0.04; data/studies/unpriced_leads/team/rhythm_body/novelty.json)
pool_rows: none (edge_anatomy scout idea #12, never built; U-161 covers team ties only)
prior_evidence: None for doubles. Family prior: sets_14d beats the close in 10 of 10 tour-eras (edge_anatomy; 2013-24 z men +3.5, women +4.0); U-138 matches already played here +3.29 beyond the model (feature_interactions, 2014-24, descriptive).
exposed_2025_26: partly: the lens (schedule-and-body unpriced in 2025-26) comes from edge_anatomy's 2025-26 ledger; no 2025-26 result of this statistic was read
notes: Register two-sided unless discovery fixes the sign (rhythm + against fatigue -). Same-day doubles excluded (order unknown). Matches where either man played doubles in the 7 days before fell from 0.47 (2018) to 0.27 (2025-26): covariate shift. TennisLive's ITF doubles enter from 2020 (tour-level doubles rows stable at about 1,900 a year plus 504 at the Slams), so a 7-day count can rise from 2020 for coverage alone: count tour and Challenger doubles only, or flag the ITF part. Bet time needs a doubles results feed (TennisLive collector exists).

name: Doubles-aware rust: surface layoff counting doubles
definition: L_any = days since the player's last match, singles or doubles, on this surface; x = [log1p(surf_layoff singles) - log1p(L_any)]_A - same_B, the rust the singles record overstates; an any-surface version beside U-132.
mechanism: Surface rust is unpriced (surf_layoff, in the model) but is measured from singles only; doubles on the surface reduce real rust while the market, like the model, reads the singles record.
data_paths: data/dump/points/tennislive/listed.parquet (discipline, start_utc, player1_members, player2_members); data/studies/lower_level_evidence/system/stage0/C0_now/evidence/crosswalk_tennislive.csv (names to Stage 0 ids); data/dump/matches/sackmann_archive/atp/atp_matches_doubles_2010..2020.parquet; data/dump/points/wta/ (API doubles 2019-26); Stage 0 surface; TennisLive event surface
coverage_note: Non-zero only where doubles fall after the last singles match on the surface: expected a few per cent of matches (to count)
prior_evidence: surf_layoff loses to the close: 2013-24 z men -1.6, women -3.0 (edge_anatomy, an in-model input)
notes: A member of the RB01 bundle; low prevalence limits its power alone

name: Rest in hours before the match (short turnaround)
definition: rest_h = this match's start (UTC; at bet time the scheduled start from the order of play) minus the end of the player's previous played match (Flashscore end_utc, else its start plus Stage 0 minutes), any level; x = s(rest_A) - s(rest_B) with s(h) = max(0, 24 - h)/24; variants 1[rest < 20 h] and log hours.
mechanism: Players, bettors and models count days; a night finish followed by an early start costs sleep and recovery that 'played yesterday' does not distinguish, and lines are set the evening before.
data_paths: data/studies/match_timing/links/flashscore.parquet + flashscore_records.parquet (start_utc, end_utc); links sofascore, live_tennis_api, api_tennis, wta_api, slam_feeds, tdi (start_utc); data/studies/predictability_diagnostic/stage0_matches.parquet (minutes, status); data/studies/match_timing/timing.parquet (obs)
coverage_note: Both players' rest in hours: men 0.90-0.97 of frame matches (2013-26), women 0.37-0.39 (2013-17) and 0.70-0.97 (2018-26). A player under 20 h in 4-9% of matches; within 72 h, 6.7% of player-matches are under 20 h and 28% under 24 h. Flashscore end_utc is missing for most men's 2025-26 matches (start + minutes used). (data/studies/unpriced_leads/team/rhythm_body/prevalence.txt)
model_overlap: low (rough x: R2 0.029 men / 0.023 women; corr with sets_14d 0.07-0.08)
pool_rows: U-132 (days, tied at the close); U-139; U-291; U-195 (start time, never tested)
prior_evidence: Days-based rest and minutes kernels unresolved beyond the close (B-LOAD z +0.63, B-PREV -0.07, 2014-24, feature_interactions); hours never built. Recalled, not verified here: sleep restriction lowers tennis serve accuracy (Reyner and Horne 2013).
notes: BetOnline's last line is recorded more than 6 h before the start for 10-15% of 2023-26 matches (bet_timing frame): drop or flag matches whose line predates the previous match's end, or late information will look unpriced for the wrong reason.

name: Same-round turnaround gap between the two players
definition: When both players' previous matches ended within 72 h: x = clip(rest_h_A - rest_h_B, -36, 36)/12, else 0; secondary: the same restricted to equal rest in days (the day-session against night-session gap).
mechanism: Nobody quotes the opponent's rest in hours; a day-session winner and a night-session winner meet the next day 10-12 h apart in recovery.
data_paths: data/studies/match_timing/links/flashscore.parquet + flashscore_records.parquet (start_utc, end_utc); links sofascore, live_tennis_api, api_tennis, wta_api, slam_feeds, tdi (start_utc); data/studies/predictability_diagnostic/stage0_matches.parquet (minutes, status); data/studies/match_timing/timing.parquet (obs)
coverage_note: Both under 72 h in 0.40-0.46 of men's frame matches (women 0.38-0.46 from 2018); gap of 12 h or more in 7-11% (men) and 8-12% (women 2018-26); gap median 2.8 h, P75 6.8 h, P90 23 h
model_overlap: low (R2 0.014 men / 0.012 women; corr with sets_14d -0.03)
prior_evidence: None for hours; days since the last match tied at the close (Stage 4 days_since)
notes: The stale-line caveat of RB03 applies

name: Recovery ratio after a long match
definition: For previous matches of 150 minutes or more: r = rest_h / (previous match minutes / 60); x = [log(1 + 1/r)]_A - same_B (0 when the previous match was shorter or rest exceeds 72 h).
mechanism: Muscle damage and glycogen loss scale with duration: 4 hours then 18 hours is not 1 hour then 18 hours; the market sees the long match, not the ratio.
data_paths: data/studies/match_timing/links/flashscore.parquet + flashscore_records.parquet (start_utc, end_utc); links sofascore, live_tennis_api, api_tennis, wta_api, slam_feeds, tdi (start_utc); data/studies/predictability_diagnostic/stage0_matches.parquet (minutes, status); data/studies/match_timing/timing.parquet (obs)
coverage_note: A previous match of 180+ min (men) or 150+ (women) in 5-8% of player-matches (feature_interactions round0 body counts, 2013-21)
prior_evidence: Previous match length tied at the close (Stage 4)
notes: Bundle member of RB03

name: Late finish then early start (event-relative)
definition: late = 1[the player's previous match was the last to end on its day at its event] (time-zone free) x 1[this match is first or second on its court today]; x = late_A - late_B.
mechanism: Night sessions and rain backlogs push finishes past midnight; the next day's early slot is a sleep deficit that the day count hides.
data_paths: data/studies/match_timing/links/flashscore.parquet + flashscore_records.parquet (start_utc, end_utc); links sofascore, live_tennis_api, api_tennis, wta_api, slam_feeds, tdi (start_utc); data/studies/predictability_diagnostic/stage0_matches.parquet (minutes, status); data/studies/match_timing/timing.parquet (obs); court and order from the Slam feeds and the WTA API (court_id)
coverage_note: Court order only for Slams and WTA API matches; 'last to end' computable wherever end times exist
prior_evidence: none
notes: A variant of RB03

name: Heat stress x heat acclimatisation
definition: H = max(0, WBGT - 25 C) over the match's hours for outdoor matches (WBGT from hourly temperature, humidity, radiation and wind at the venue; 0 indoors); Acc_X = sum over X's matches in the 14 days before of max(0, WBGT_j - 22) exp(-days_j / 7); x = H (Acc_A - Acc_B) / sd.
mechanism: Both players face the same heat, so prices move little; acclimatisation builds over one to two weeks and depends on where a player came from (indoor Europe or clay to Australia or the US summer), which no line tracks.
data_paths: download: Open-Meteo archive (probe receipt data/studies/unpriced_leads/team/rhythm_body/probes/); a venue gazetteer to build (211 frame venue names, 816 Challenger names; cities in data/dump/points/wta/editions.parquet and data/dump/matches/open_tennis_data/tournaments.parquet); start times as RB03
coverage_note: Men's frame matches 84% outdoor; hot sessions concentrate in January (Australia), February-April (Americas, Gulf) and July-September (North America, Asia); the WTA log flags heat breaks in 14-52 matches a year (2019-26)
pool_rows: U-196 (needs new data; register C01 untested)
prior_evidence: None in the repository. Recalled, not verified here: heat acclimatisation physiology (Periard, Racinais and Sawka 2015) and heat-related retirements at the Australian Open.
notes: ERA5 grid (about 25 km) against the venue's microclimate; roofs and night sessions; at bet time use the forecast WBGT of the scheduled slot. The ATP heat rule from 2026 (provider claim via edge_anatomy's scout) is a structural change.

name: Heat tolerance trait: home climate and body size in the heat
definition: x = H (Clim_A - Clim_B) / sd with Clim = the mean summer WBGT of the player's country (Stage 0 country; training base where known); companions H (height_A - height_B) and H (age_A - age_B).
mechanism: Heat tolerance differs with the climate a player is used to and with body size; the market prices famous cases, not the gradient.
data_paths: data/studies/predictability_diagnostic/stage0_match_players.parquet (country, height, age); climate normals by country (download, small) or from the Open-Meteo archive
coverage_note: Country near-complete; women's height 39-64% in recent seasons
prior_evidence: none in the repository
notes: Nation represented is not residence

name: Women's heat-break and medical history (WTA umpire log)
definition: For women: shrunk count of the player's matches in the last 12 months with a heat break (reason HeatBreak10Minutes or Heat) or a physio or medical treatment; x = diff, and H x that history.
mechanism: Who needed treatment in the heat before is a direct sensitivity label the market does not compile.
data_paths: data/dump/points/wta/events/<year>.parquet (type, reason)
coverage_note: 2,300-6,300 logged matches a year (2019-26); heat breaks in 14-52 a year; physio called in 584-956 matches a year (2021-26)
prior_evidence: A physio treatment in the previous match: retirement risk ratio 2.27, but results barely move (point_sequence)
notes: Women only; low counts

name: Style-specific ageing: age x the return share of the long-memory edge
definition: Drift_X = (age_X - 29)+ x RS_X, RS_X = Dbar / (|Obar| + |Dbar|), Obar and Dbar the means of X's standardised per-surface IOS offence and defence values (per-player store columns pp__ios_srf*), optionally x the profile's memory (years since its median match); x = Drift_A - Drift_B.
mechanism: Movement and return skills fade earlier than serving; the market prices 'veteran' as one number and the long-memory profile lags decline, so ageing returners stay over-rated. The model sees age only as A - B and cannot apply A's own curve.
data_paths: data/studies/feature_universe/store.parquet (pp__ios_srfO_*_a/_b, pp__ios_srfD_*_a/_b); stage0_match_players.parquet (age); data/studies/match_timing/leakproof_features.parquet
coverage_note: Men's player-matches aged 30+: 31% (2013-21); men's matches with a player aged 32+: 38% (2017-19), 21% (2025-26) (edge_anatomy scout)
pool_rows: none (BOD-27, proposed 6 Oct, never built); U-294 (height x age) related
prior_evidence: Age loses to the close: men z -3.3 (2013-24, edge_anatomy); B-AGE (age x form gap) failed replication. Outcome-free gate: per-statistic ageing curves on box scores of seasons <= 2024.
exposed_2025_26: partly: age's 2025-26 ledger reading (men z -2.0) seen
notes: Tension with edge_anatomy's 2025-26 'returners under-rated': the ageing term predicts the opposite, for older returners only; decide on <= 2024

name: Career mileage beyond age (full careers)
definition: Odo_X = log(1 + career matches at every level up to the match) minus its age-expected value (fitted on cohorts before 2013); x = [(age - 27)+ Odo]_A - same_B and Odo_A - Odo_B.
mechanism: Wear: at equal age, more career matches means an older body; the market prices age, not mileage.
data_paths: Stage 0 (2010 on); Sackmann's archive before 2010 (download, public); data/dump/players/tennis_my_life/ATP_Database.parquet (turnedpro, men)
coverage_note: Careers begun before 2010 are truncated on disk
pool_rows: U-158 (played_career: tied, flagged a warm-up artefact of truncation); U-169 (turnedpro)
prior_evidence: U-158 tied at the close on a truncated history (feature_universe)
exposed_2025_26: partly: U-158 was scored on windows that include 2025-26
notes: Years since turning pro (men, static) is a cheap proxy

name: Years past the player's own peak
definition: Peak_X = the maximum of X's overall Elo to date; YPP_X = years since it; x = [(age - 27)+ min(YPP, 5)]_A - same_B; companion: the 24-month slope of the level.
mechanism: After a peak, decline tends to continue; ratings and reputations lag it.
data_paths: Stage 1 Elo (store columns m__elo_overall; per-player Elo history from the Stage 1 builder)
coverage_note: all frame matches
pool_rows: U-045 (career-peak Elo and the fall from it); U-270 (I-083 fallen-star premium)
prior_evidence: Elo change over 26/52 weeks made close-based forecasts worse for men (U-028); B-REPUTE's windows disagree in sign
notes: Weak prior; listed to cover 'age against the player's own curve'

name: Qualifier and lucky-loser arrival cost
definition: For a qualifier or lucky loser in the first main-draw match: Qcost = log1p(points played in this event's qualifying), Qrest = hours since the qualifying final ended (as RB03), LL = 1[lucky loser]; x = Qcost_A - Qcost_B (0 for direct entrants); secondary LL x On (U-138).
mechanism: The market prices the Q tag ('the dangerous qualifier', match-tight) but not what the run cost or how little rest followed. LL against Q separates on-site rhythm (both have it) from survival (the LL lost).
data_paths: stage0_match_players.parquet (entry; tpw_d for points played); stage0_matches.parquet (qualifying, round, minutes); clock times as RB03
coverage_note: A Q or LL in 19-31% of frame matches (men GS 0.19, 250s 0.27; women GS 0.12, 250s and 500s 0.30-0.31); their rest: P10 21.5 h, P25 24 h, median 41 h
pool_rows: U-176 (entry type, ties at the close); U-276 (INFO-2 qualifying form, never screened alone); U-138
prior_evidence: Q entry beats surface Elo (onE men +0.40) but ties at the close (Stage 4)
exposed_2025_26: partly: U-176 was scored on windows that include 2025-26
notes: The LL contrast is a mechanism probe for U-138

name: The bye seed's cold start against an opponent with on-site matches
definition: At events with first-round byes (draws 28, 48, 56, 96): in the bye seed's first match, x = log1p(On_opponent) x log1p(days since the seed's last match), signed toward the seed; else 0.
mechanism: The expanded 12-day 1000s made bye-seed matches common; the opponent has played here, the seed has only practised.
data_paths: stage0_matches.parquet (draw_size, round, tournament_id); stage0_match_players.parquet (seed); the U-138 builder (src/eda/feature_interactions/features/f24_onsite.py)
coverage_note: 1000s matches at 96 draws: about 33% (2013-22), 86% men / 80% women (2025-26); a seed meets an unseeded player with more matches here in 33-43% (edge_anatomy scout)
prior_evidence: U-138 +3.29 beyond the model (2014-24, descriptive); I-076 +0.99
exposed_2025_26: partly: the lens (schedule-and-body unpriced in 2025-26) comes from edge_anatomy's 2025-26 ledger; no 2025-26 result of this statistic was read
notes: A population refinement of a pool item (edge_anatomy scout #3)

name: Recent retirement or walkover given, any level, without a long break
definition: R28_X = 1[X retired or gave a walkover in any match in the 28 days before, with no 42+ day break since]; x = R28_A - R28_B; companion count over 90 days.
mechanism: A player back within weeks of a retirement is a health question that the model reads as a short rest; the earlier test used a truncated main-tour-only history.
data_paths: stage0_matches.parquet (status, every level); stage0_match_players.parquet
coverage_note: About 1.5% of main-tour player-matches follow the player's retirement in the previous match (2013-21, feature_interactions round0 body counts)
pool_rows: U-136 (only before 6-week breaks); U-160 (frontier, tied, truncated history); U-178
prior_evidence: U-160 tied on a truncated history; I-043's rust was stronger after a retirement or walkover given before the break (descriptive)
exposed_2025_26: partly: B-INJ (with this injury flag) was tested once on 2025-26, unresolved
notes: Rare: power only inside a health bundle

name: Withdrawal from an entered event in the last five weeks
definition: W35_X = 1[X withdrew from an event whose main draw began in the 35 days before], split by stated reason (injury or illness against other); x = W35_A - W35_B.
mechanism: The singles record shows the gap as rest; a withdrawal for injury says it was not. News covers top players, not the rest of the draw.
data_paths: download: Wikipedia tournament pages (Withdrawals sections), ATP and WTA entry lists
coverage_note: Unknown; about 1,800 main-tour event pages for 2013-26
prior_evidence: none
notes: The completeness of the reason field decides its value

name: Conditions-matched rust: same surface, indoor status and court pace
definition: CM_X = log1p(days since X's last match with the same surface, the same indoor status and a venue pace within one SD of this venue's), capped at 365; x = CM_A - CM_B beside the model's surf_layoff; companion: an altitude band (1,000 m or more) in the matching key.
mechanism: The surface label hides indoor against outdoor, fast against slow and altitude; surface rust is unpriced in the model, and the finer adaptation cost is less visible still.
data_paths: stage0_matches.parquet (surface, indoor for men); women's indoor status (src/eda/indoor_fill/status.py); venue pace U-192 (src/eda/feature_interactions/features/f09_venue.py); an altitude table (download, about 15 venues)
coverage_note: Lower-level venues lack pace and, for women, indoor flags
prior_evidence: Switch states tied: B-SWITCH Wald p 0.31, I-075 +0.10, novelty null (feature_interactions, 2014-24); surf_layoff is unpriced (in model)
timing_class: needs_clock (venue pace is a field statistic; leak-proof U-192 passed the probe)
notes: Negative priors on switch states: keep only if it beats surf_layoff on <= 2024

name: Altitude arrival
definition: At venues of 1,000 m or more: x = [log1p(days on site at altitude)]_A - same_B; companion: altitude x (iosO_ace_A - iosO_ace_B).
mechanism: Thin air speeds the ball; players just down from sea level need days; venue character is known, adaptation is not.
data_paths: an elevation table (download, small); Stage 0
coverage_note: About 400 matches a tour (2013-21) at Bogota, Quito, Gstaad, Guadalajara (feature_interactions round0 body counts)
prior_evidence: none (register C04 untested)
notes: Tiny sample; better as a member of RB17

name: Real time-zone shift with days to adapt and direction
definition: dz = the UTC offset of this venue minus that of the player's previous match venue (city-level table with daylight saving); T = days from that match to this one; JL = |dz| max(0, 1 - T/|dz|), x 1.5 eastward; x = JL_A - JL_B.
mechanism: Circadian adaptation takes about a day per zone; no line does the arithmetic of zones and days.
data_paths: a city-level gazetteer (download); Stage 0; the clock
coverage_note: First matches within 7 days of an event on another continent: 1,103 men's and 821 women's (2013-21, feature_interactions round0 body counts)
pool_rows: U-151 (continent-level proxy offsets, inside B10, tied); U-305
notes: Better data for a tied block; low prior

name: Excess on-site cost (struggle against cruise)
definition: Ex_X = log1p(points played at this event before today) minus its expectation given the number of on-site matches, best of, tour and surface (fitted on seasons before 2013); x = Ex_A - Ex_B.
mechanism: Two-sided: real fatigue (-) or the market over-reading a struggle as decline (+).
data_paths: stage0_match_players.parquet (tpw_d); stage0_matches.parquet
coverage_note: Defined from the second match at an event (about 57% of player-matches)
pool_rows: U-142; U-289 (B-PREV, tied); BOD-01's Ex (never built)

name: Slam physical cost from tracking: distance run in earlier rounds beyond minutes
definition: Dist_X = metres run by X in this Slam's earlier rounds (US Open per set) residualised on minutes and sets; x = Dist_A - Dist_B.
mechanism: Score lines and durations are public, running is not; two three-hour matches differ in physical cost by style and opponent.
data_paths: data/dump/points/usopen/distance.parquet; data/dump/points/usopen/matches.parquet; other Slams' tracking to derive or download
coverage_note: US Open 2022-26 only: 1,652 matches with distance
prior_evidence: none
notes: Underpowered alone; fits the owner's point-level thesis

name: Serve-speed fade in the previous match (men)
definition: fade_X = first-serve speed in the last set of X's previous match minus its first set, minus X's own typical fade (shrunk); x = fade_A - fade_B.
mechanism: A speed drop late in a match is a fatigue or injury sensor that no score line shows.
data_paths: data/dump/points/infosys_atp/ (rally: serveSpeed per point); data/dump/points/infosys_slams/; decrypted Stats Centre files
coverage_note: Men, tour level, 2021-26 where per-point speeds exist
prior_evidence: spd_L (stage 2) unstable; fade never built
notes: Cross-lens with B2

name: Short off-season after a late finish to the previous season
definition: For a player's first three matches of a season: Off_X = days between his last match of the previous season and his first of this season; x = [log Off]_A - same_B; companion: pre-season match play (United Cup, exhibitions).
mechanism: Finals and Davis Cup Finals players lose their training block; the market sees ranking, not the calendar.
data_paths: Stage 0 (all levels incl. TEAM); data/studies/match_timing/links/flashscore_records.parquet (is_exhibition)
coverage_note: Each player's first matches of the season
pool_rows: U-133 - U-135 (rust after a break; off-season returns carry about 60% of I-043)

name: Alive in the doubles draw (future load)
definition: 1[the player's doubles team is still in this event's draw when the singles match starts], from results before it; x = diff; strongest at Slams and in late rounds.
mechanism: Two draws compete for one body late in the week; invisible to singles pricing.
data_paths: data/dump/points/tennislive/listed.parquet (discipline, start_utc, player1_members, player2_members); data/studies/lower_level_evidence/system/stage0/C0_now/evidence/crosswalk_tennislive.csv (names to Stage 0 ids); data/dump/matches/sackmann_archive/atp/atp_matches_doubles_2010..2020.parquet; data/dump/points/wta/ (API doubles 2019-26)
coverage_note: As RB01
prior_evidence: none
notes: A member of the RB01 bundle

name: Team-event doubles rubbers and tie travel
definition: Team_X = doubles rubbers at Davis Cup, BJK Cup and United Cup ties in the 21 days before (singles rubbers are already in sets_14d) plus 1[the tie was on another continent]; x = diff.
mechanism: Tour form guides leave out team ties' doubles and travel.
data_paths: Stage 0 TEAM singles rubbers (5,067 men's, 4,239 women's); doubles rubbers not held (download)
coverage_note: Mostly February and September ties, United Cup in January
prior_evidence: none

name: Exhibition match play
definition: Exhibition matches in the 21 days before (Six Kings Slam, UTS, Kooyong, World Tennis League and others flagged as exhibitions); x = diff.
mechanism: Match play outside the official record; the market sees the headline, not the load.
data_paths: data/studies/match_timing/links/flashscore_records.parquet (is_exhibition)
coverage_note: 22-70 exhibition records a year outside 2020-21 (9,780 in 2020)
prior_evidence: none
notes: Too sparse to test alone
